body:
Fix the non-propagating (blocked) Garner drag so it matches GFDL topo_drag: accumulate the WKB phase
  as Σ Δz·N/V_τ, use each cell's own pressure thickness with wtsum = Σ Δp·weight, and start the blocked
  layer in the first level above the PBL (GFDL kpbl). The old phase used height above the PBL at every
  face, and wtsum divided instead of multiplying, which made the blocked layer too shallow and the
  tendency unphysically large (saturating the ±3e-3 clamp over topography).

  Add Beljaars (2004) turbulent orographic form drag (TOFD) in its IFS form (du/dt = −C_d(z)|U|u), the
  near-surface drag that the propagating and blocked components (above the PBL top) do not provide. Its
  input σ_flt is computed at initialization from the 60″ ETOPO orography with the IFS band-pass
  filter, and it is applied every step in backward-Euler form. Controlled by ogw_tofd_coefficient
  (a_tofd, ClimaParams 1.3.8): 1 = IFS strength, 0 = off.

  Replace the per-component ±3e-3 clamp with a single vector-magnitude limit at 3e-3·√2 (diagonal of
  the old box), so the drag direction is preserved when the limiter binds and the cap is no tighter
  than before in any direction.
title: OGW: fix blocked drag, add Beljaars TOFD, preserve clamp direction

## Purpose 
<!--- One sentence to describe the purpose of this PR, refer to any linked issues:
#14 -- this will link to issue 14
Closes #2 -- this will automatically close issue 2 on PR merge
-->
- Remove the `linear` case in orographic gravity wave.
- Fix the non-orographic gravity wave break criteria, which started one level below the launch level and dropped the flux of any wave that broke there.
- Fix the redistribution of flux that escapes the model top, which redistributed it by level count instead of by level mass, so the momentum redistributed did not match the momentum that escaped.
- Add unit test for AD99's momentum budget.


<!---  list of proposed tasks in the PR, move to "Content" on completion 
- Proposed task
- ## To-do
-->

## Content
<!---  specific tasks that are currently complete 
- Solution implemented
-->
A column should deposit exactly the momentum the scheme launches. It did not. Two independent leaks were responsible.

**1. Off-by-one at the launch level.** The break/reflection test looped from `source_level_eff - 1` upward, but both the deposition (`fm += B0[n]`) and the flux-to-acceleration conversion were triggered by `level >= source_level_eff`.
So in that one extra level, a wave could be removed from the spectrum while its momentum flux went nowhere. The loop now starts at `source_level_eff` everywhere, so a wave that is already unstable at its own launch level
deposits into the first layer rather than being discarded.

**2. Escaped flux was redistributed by count, not by mass.** Flux that reached the model top without breaking was force-broken there, and `gw_deposit` redistributed it as `wave_forcing_top / (height + 2 - damp_level)`, i.e. the top
acceleration divided by one more than the number of receiving levels. However, the average receiving level's mass differs substantially from the ghost top, so the momentum deposited did not equal the momentum that escaped.

**Verification.** New unit test `test_ad99_momentum_budget.jl` checks the column budget against a closed form, `F_launch = source_ampl · Σ B0 / Σ |B0|`, which is independent of the density profile, the wind profile, the grid, and the number of phase-speed bins. Three cases isolate the three places the equality can fail: the interior conversion and half-level-to-cell remap, the escaped-flux redistribution, and deletion at the source level.

Note that the one remaining place momentum is not conserved is the ±3e-3 m s⁻² clip applied per component when the forcing is added to the momentum tendency. Where that clip is active the deposited momentum is smaller than the launched momentum by construction.
